Team — forwarding Brightleaf's note and their usage CSV (attached in original). Quick status: customer renewed July 1 on a committed plan; there was unplanned spike Jul 15–25. They'd like a one-time settlement instead of raising the committed baseline.

Key asks:
- Marcus: can you model a settlement that applies a partial credit for experimental traffic and invoices the remainder as a one-time retro charge? We should show both: (a) full overage billed, (b) an alternative with a 40% experimental credit — per previous precedent with ProHealth last year.
- Lauren: confirm contractual terms around post-term adjustments (I think our T&C allow retroactive billing through 30 days of usage checks).
- Marissa: if we offer a one-time invoice, what internal GL code do we use and can finance emit the invoice by Aug 12?

Thanks — hop on quick if needed.

—Kim

Subject: Proposal: one-time settlement + optional capacity conversion (Brightleaf)

Alex / Jordan — thanks for the patience. Per internal review, please find our proposed settlement:

Proposal summary:
- Gross overage (Jul 15–25): $34,740
- Experimental credit (40% applied to test-run buckets): -$13,896
- Net one-time invoice: $20,844
- Option A (recommended): Apply $10,000 of the net invoice toward additional committed capacity for the remainder of 2026, resulting in a one-time billed amount of $10,844 and a committed uplift of 2K concurrent tokens equivalent (applied immediately).
- Option B: Straight one-time invoice for $20,844 (billed within 7 days).

If you prefer Option A we will:
- Issue DocuSign amendment to append the one-time committed uplift to the renewal (no change to term end date).
- Issue a one-time invoice for the residual amount.

Please confirm by Aug 12 so finance can finalize the invoice and we can get the DocuSign executed. I attached the settlement worksheet and a draft invoice for clarity.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
